langCode.description: BCP 47 code of this translation: used for <html lang> and number/date formatting

extName.description: Extension name in Chrome Web Store and chrome://extensions (max 75 chars)

extDescription.message: Save 2FA keys from QR codes on a page or in images and copy TOTP codes in one click. Offline, with an optional password.

scanBtnTitle.message: Find a QR code on the current page

emptyHint.message: Open a page with a 2FA QR code and click “Scan page”, paste a QR image right here ($1), or import a Google Authenticator export via “Keys…”.

emptyLocalNote.message: Keys are stored only in this browser profile and never leave your device.

saveAndCopyTitle.message: Save the key and copy the current code: the site asks for it right away

scrollHint.message: If the QR code is off-screen, scroll to it. Or copy the QR image and press $1 here.

scanning.message: Looking for a QR code on the page…

pwTooShort.message: The password must be at least $1 characters

errBase32Chars.message: The key has characters outside base32 (A–Z, 2–7)

errNoSecret.message: The link has no valid secret (base32)

errNotOtp.message: Doesn't look like otpauth:// or otpauth-migration://

errTruncated.message: The export data is truncated or damaged

errNoData.message: The otpauth-migration link has no data parameter

errMd5.message: MD5 isn't supported by Web Crypto

gaIncompatPeriod.message: period $1 s: the Google format only stores 30 s

gaIncompatDigits.message: $1 digits: the Google format only supports 6 and 8

dropRest.message: , click to choose files, or paste with $1.

dropHint.message: Works with 2FA setup QR codes (otpauth://) and Google Authenticator exports (otpauth-migration://), several files at once.

restoreTitle.message: A AuthBackup backup (plain or encrypted) or a .txt with otpauth:// links

expGoogleTitle.message: One or more otpauth-migration:// QR codes, the same as “Transfer accounts” in Google Authenticator

expOtpauthTitle.message: Text file with one otpauth:// link per line; Aegis, 2FAS, Bitwarden and others can read it

notAffiliated.message: AuthBackup is an independent project, not affiliated with Google. Google Authenticator is a trademark of Google LLC.

noQrInImage.message: No QR code found in the image

secretNotBase32.message: The secret must be base32: A–Z and 2–7

detailsScanHint.message: Scan this QR code with your phone to move the key.

confirmDelete.message:
Delete “$1”?
The key will be lost unless you have it somewhere else.

gaHowOne.message: In the app: “Transfer accounts” → “Import accounts”, then scan this QR code.

gaHowMany.message: In the app: “Transfer accounts” → “Import accounts”, then scan all the QR codes one by one.

gaNone.message: None of the selected keys can be transferred in this format.

gaShaWarn.message: SHA256/SHA512 ($1): some versions of Google Authenticator compute these codes as SHA1, so check the code after the transfer.

gaSkipped.message: Not included: $1. You can transfer them one at a time via “Key / QR”.

gaSecretWarn.message: These QR codes contain your secrets. Don't take screenshots or show them on video calls.

encHintProtected.message: The file is encrypted with your password. Enter it: you'll need the same password to restore.

encHintNew.message: It decrypts the file when you restore. Without it the backup is useless.

exportedPlain.message: Keys exported: $1. The file is plain text, keep it as safe as a password

notBackup.message: This isn't a AuthBackup backup or a list of otpauth:// links

secOnText.message: Your keys are encrypted with AES-256-GCM using a key derived from your password with PBKDF2-SHA256 ($1 iterations). After you unlock, the key stays in browser memory until auto-lock or until Chrome closes.

secOffText.message: No password yet: keys are stored unencrypted in your Chrome profile. With a password the keys are encrypted (AES-256-GCM) and codes are shown only after you unlock. It locks after inactivity, with the button, and when the browser closes.

pwWarn.message: A forgotten password can't be recovered, and the keys are lost with it. Make an export or an encrypted backup first.

removePwHint.message: Keys will be stored unencrypted in your Chrome profile again.

noteProtected.message: Keys are encrypted with your password and never leave this device. Plain export files (JSON, otpauth) contain the secrets as is.

noteOpen.message: Secrets are stored unencrypted in chrome.storage.local of this Chrome profile and never leave this device. Plain export files contain the secrets as is.

copiesTitle.message: 2+1: keep your keys in three places

copyAppHaveTitle.message: These keys are already in an authenticator on your phone or in a password manager

copyFileMissing.message: File or cloud — keys without a copy: $1

copyMailHint.message: Put the file on a drive or email it to yourself. Only its password protects it, so make the password long.

copiesDoneTitle.message: Browser, phone app and a file or cloud copy. Open export

emptyRule.message: Rule 2+1: keep 2FA keys in three places: here, in an app on your phone and in an encrypted file.

copiesStatusOffsite.message: File or cloud — keys without a copy: $1 ($2).
